bugs.text: updateChallengeDestroy is never called, so challenge-stage hits are never counted: the results screen always reads NUMBER OF HITS 0 / BONUS 0, and the 1,000-per-wave and 10,000 PERFECT bonuses can never be awarded.

Goei escorts never return to their slots: once the Boss is back in formation they stay attached to it at an offset inside the formation and still count as active divers, so at stages 1-2 (maxDivers = 1) no further dives launch until they are shot.

The tractor Boss pauses for only ~0.63s, then returns to the top while the beam stays on for the remaining ~1s and follows it; the beam is also active from the moment of launch, so the player can be captured while the Boss is still at formation height.
Title score table: '150 / 400 / 800 / 1600' is 131px wide starting at x=118 and overflows the 224px canvas; '1600' is clipped (1-title.png).
Stage badges are one flag per threshold, not a denomination sum (stage 2 shows one '1' flag, stage 7 shows '5' and '1'); the digit on the 8px flag is unreadable.
Star scrolling advances per rendered frame inside drawStars, so the starfield speed depends on the monitor's refresh rate.

All 40 enemies fire on independent 1.5-3.5s timers from the moment they spawn (60% chance while entering), so stage 1 has ~20 enemy bullets on screen at 5s (2-after-enter-5s.png); the play-test bot lost all three ships twice inside 45s.
A captured fighter stays at the formation slot while its Boss dives instead of flying with it; the rescue animation starts from the slot, not from the Boss.
When the dual fighter has only one shot slot free it fires a single shot from the centre, between the two hulls.
Entering enemies fly to the unswayed baseX and then snap to the swayed slot position on arrival (up to 3.5px jump).
sfxEnemyHit is dead code; non-Boss hits play only the destroyed sound.

summary: A tidy, readable single file: one state object, update functions kept apart from draw functions, a true fixed-step loop, pixel font and sprites as data, and a full Web Audio set including an LFO-modulated beam drone. Most of the Galaga ruleset is present and wired up: curved group entries, a swaying and breathing 40-enemy formation, two-hit colour-changing Bosses with escort-multiplied scores, dives that wrap from the bottom back to the slot, a working capture/rescue/dual-fighter chain, challenge stages, and the hit-miss results screen; the play-test ran clean with no console errors. Faithfulness suffers in the details: Zako and Goei share one sprite in two colours and the 'wing flap' is a one-pixel bob, the tractor Boss barely pauses and drags its beam back up the screen, escorts never rejoin the formation and silently stall dives on early stages, the challenge-stage hit counter is never called so NUMBER OF HITS and the PERFECT bonus are dead, badges are threshold flags rather than denominations, and the stage-1 bullet density is far above the arcade's. It plays as a competent, fast and rather harsh Galaga-like with a few rules that quietly do not work.
